solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: in places the word for tip inside the word for exchange

parts.note: to barter is to exchange goods
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: A waiter is handed a gratuity as part of some deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a gratuity for the server, but it is END, a point or extremity, placed in BARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks behind a bar, so is a server.

clue.text: Go off booklet at regular intervals

indicators.note: at regular intervals takes every other letter of booklet, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone storms away from a pamphlet, or a pamphlet goes bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run off suddenly, to go off in a hurry.

indicators.note: for a listener, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: writs are formal legal documents

explanation.surface: Paperwork from a hotel is handed over for the accounts inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant checking books; here it is simply a listener, so WRITS is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London (and elsewhere).

clue.text: Pleased inside to have bird from the Orient

indicators.note: inside takes letters from within the word Pleased

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to keep a bird imported from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pleased' looks like part of the surface's happy mood; its inner letters EAS start the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern means coming from the East, which is what the Orient is.

indicators.note: inside signals letters concealed within the words citadel talking

explanation.surface: Someone notable is chatting within a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and letters are characters.

parts.note: read as a state: in good health now, having been ill, rather than the conversational filler

explanation.surface: A conversational opener, as in 'well now, let me see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having recovered from an illness means being well again now.

clue.text: Fabulous writer having a retrogressive attitude

indicators.note: retrogressive means going backwards, so the word for attitude is read in reverse

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or stance

explanation.surface: An author of tales holds old-fashioned, backward-looking views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like praise; here it means writing fables. 'retrogressive' turns the attitude word round to give ESOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek author of fables, hence a writer of fables.

clue.text: Opposed to a profit over the way

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the earlier pieces above the last one

parts.note: gain is profit
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone objects to making money over a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is a preposition meaning in opposition to.

clue.text: In jug skimp exercising for winter sport

indicators.note: exercising suggests the letters are worked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trains by skimping on drinks, getting ready for the cold season's sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski jumping is a Winter Olympic sport.

clue.text: Clergyman appears before a railway goes round corner

indicators.note: goes round means the first pieces enclose the word for corner

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a bend in a road is a corner

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows up ahead of a train line that curves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is only a link; the image of a railway curving round a corner is the container instruction 'goes round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prebendary is a canon of a cathedral, a member of the clergy.

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: comes first puts the word for fortune ahead of the abbreviation

parts.note: your lot is your fortune or fate

explanation.surface: Lily's American fortune is her top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a woman's name; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, the sacred flower of Asia.

clue.text: Endless good fortune with four in charge moneymaking

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for good fortune is dropped

parts.note: luck is good fortune

indicators.note: in places the Roman four inside the word for charge

parts.note: a rate is a charge or price
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Constant luck, with four people in control, brings in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' looks like one phrase meaning in control, but 'in' is the container signal and 'charge' supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative means profitable, making money.

clue.text: According to notice put at risk by chance

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per instructions'
an ad is a notice or advertisement
to venture is to risk something

explanation.surface: According to an advert, something was gambled by luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic word meaning perhaps, by chance.

parts.note: carbon is a chemical element
ate means consumed
D is short for daughter; 'by' places it alongside

explanation.surface: A girl swallows a fizzing chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonated drinks have carbon dioxide dissolved in them, making them fizzy.

parts.note: a dummy is a sham, not the real thing
whist is a classic trick-taking card game

explanation.surface: A card game that is somehow not genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: In this whist variant one hand is a dummy played openly, so the 'unreal' player is part of the game itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummy whist is a version of whist for three, with one hand laid open as a dummy.

clue.text: A learner with students accepted word of hesitation from old boy

parts.note: L is for learner, as on an L-plate
um is the sound people make while hesitating
NUS is the National Union of Students, a British body

explanation.surface: A learner and students let a former pupil hesitate.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former pupil of a school or college, what the British call an old boy.

clue.text: Type of PIN on the web provides means of protection

parts.note: a safety pin is one type of pin
the Net is the web, the internet

explanation.surface: A kind of PIN code used online guards your security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PIN' looks like a bank code in the web context; it is a pin, the safety pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety net is a backup that protects against failure.

parts.note: a typing pool is an office of typists; making a fresh printed impression there means keying a document again

explanation.surface: Someone splashes about in a swimming pool and makes a fresh impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype is to type again, producing a new printed copy.

clue.text: Cut most of the reference lines

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the word for reference lines is dropped

parts.note: axes on a graph are reference lines

explanation.surface: Most of the reference lines are deleted.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to cut it, as with a budget or a job.

parts.note: a bump is a knock
off. is an abbreviation of official

explanation.surface: Bang out an official message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'official dispatch' looks like one phrase, a government message, but 'dispatch' is the definition, meaning kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump off is slang for to kill, and to dispatch also means to kill.

clue.text: Bulk order, it's arranged before end of day

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of it's are put in another order
end of takes the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A bulk order is arranged before the day is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulk order' reads as a large purchase; the order is the British honour, and 'arranged' gives SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity is excessive body bulk.

definitions.meaning: divine means wonderful, so the comparative adds -er
a soothsayer foretells the future or finds hidden things

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller who is even more marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: A diviner is one who divines, foretelling the future; also the comparative of divine.

parts.note: an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
taken as written
on means operating, as with a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman is running a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a pastime; it is meat from hunted animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is deer meat, which counts as game.

parts.note: the word statement rearranged afresh gives the second word, and the whole names the later half of the Bible

explanation.surface: A pronouncement from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the second part of the Christian Bible, containing the Gospels.

parts.note: a gnasher is a tooth, and the ones at the back of the mouth are the grinding kind

explanation.surface: A dog that snaps from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Molars are the grinding teeth at the back of the mouth.

parts.note: a hut is a shed; the 's means 'is'
U means acceptable to the upper class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: An African's shed passes muster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are a Bantu-speaking people of Rwanda and Burundi.

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the word for perfect is dropped

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: An idea that falls short of perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion or thought.

clue.text: Out with Latin, I challenged, it's to do with teaching

indicators.note: challenged suggests the letters are disordered into a new form

explanation.surface: Latin is out, I protested; it concerns education.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuitional is the adjective from tuition, which is teaching.

clue.text: Second one of four in working party

parts.note: a quad is one of quadruplets, one of four born together

explanation.surface: The second of four people is in a work team.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad is a small group of people working together.

definitions.meaning: covered with dots, like a spotty pattern

explanation.surface: Someone has been seen acting a bit mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means covered in dots and also, informally, mildly eccentric.

indicators.note: protected means the soldiers surround the remaining letters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the letters of natural are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Troops guard a born rebel who preys on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a rebel; it rearranges the letters of natural into ARANTUL, which 'protected' places within the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantula is a large hairy spider that hunts prey.
